the 7-azaisoindolo[2,1-c]quinoline scaffold has the greatest Top1 binding affinity, and that the introduction of a 2-methoxy substituent into the D-ring improves both the Top1 binding affinity and cytotoxicity.
the introduction of a 7-azindenoisoquinoline moiety into the D ring of a Top1 inhibitor leads to the most potent inhibitors of the series.

a series of 7-aza-1,2-dihydro-4,5,10-trimethoxy-6H-indeno[2,1-b]isoquinolines were found to possess potent Top1 inhibition and cytotoxicity, and that the binding of these compounds to the DNA cleavage complex is governed by a balance of dispersion and charge-transfer interactions between the drugs and DNA base pairs flanking the scissile bond of the DNA.

the design, synthesis, and structure-activity relationships (SAR) of azaindenoisquinolines as Top1 inhibitors and potential anticancers.
the development of a novel series of azainidenoisoquinoline derivatives with potent Top1 inhibitory and cytotoxic activities.
the development of a novel class of Top1 inhibitors, which have shown potent cytotoxic activities and are promising candidates as anticancer agents.

the 7-azindenoisoquinolines are the best Top1 inhibitors and cytotoxic agents in this series.
the Top1 inhibitory activities and cytotoxicities of azaindenoisquinolines depend on their ability to form a π-π sandwich complex with flanking base pairs in the Drug-Top-DNA ternary complexes.

a series of 10-azanidenoisquinolines with a wide spectrum of biological activities has been developed.
the 7-azanidoisoquinoline core is an excellent scaffold for the design of Top1 inhibitors.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the introduction of a nitrogen atom into the D-ring is beneficial for the Top1 inhibitory and cytotoxic activity of azaindenoisquinolines, and the presence of the methoxy group at the D-ring is also beneficial for the TopI inhibitory and cytotoxicty of azaindenisoquinolines.
the Top1 inhibitory activities of the 7-azanidenoisoquinoline derivatives are strongly correlated with the strength of the π-π interactions between the D ring and the flanking base pairs.
